Ever since its inception, the[** Master of Business Administration**](http://www.udaysalunkhewelingkar.in/uday-salunkhe-journey.php#) (MBA) has remained a lucrative education option. The degree has proved to be tenacious, as its relevance hasn’t diminished over the last century. With the evolution of the formal business world since the early 1900s, the scope of the MBA programme has only grown.

The MBA was initially devised to train business managers in skills of accountancy. “However,” says, Dr. [**Uday Salunkhe**](http://www.udaysalunkhe.co.in/online-mba.php) Group Director, Prin. L.N. Welingkar Institute of Management Research and Development (WeSchool), “The number and focus of the early MBA programmes gradually evolved along with global changes.”

By 1960s, the MBA programme was creating a new professional class of managers by coaching students in soft skills around leading teams and broadening their expertise through diverse subjects like marketing and operations, while enhancing their knowledge of financial markets.

But the [**MBA** ](http://www.udaysalunkhe.co.in/online-mba.php)went truly global by the start of the new millennium, once the international student uptake more than doubled and the gender-ratio slowly improved. Besides the study content, the classroom underwent massive transformations as well. For instance, the Welingkar institute began offering virtual classroom sessions where learned professors deliver lectures remotely from the campus studio to thousands of students across campus.

[**Welingkar**](http://www.udaysalunkhewelingkar.com/welingkar-institute.php), Mumbai, is a member institution of the Shikshana Prasaraka (S.P.) Mandali, Pune. Educational institutions of S.P. Mandali attract students from all over India as they are known for their academic excellence. Welingkar is no exception; the business school has the distinction of being the seventh best educational institute in South Asia. “The content of our programmes is interactive and comprehensive. Students are mentored by stalwarts from different walks of life for entrepreneurship and innovative thinking so that they develop into leaders with global mindsets,” informs [**Dr. Uday Salunkhe**](http://www.udaysalunkhe.com/uday-salunkhe.php).

A truly global MBA programme adds incremental value by providing graduates with opportunities to learn alongside peers from diverse cultural backgrounds. The education prepares the graduates to work with and manage multi-cultural and geographically spread teams in the future. Not only do the programmes offered by the Welingkar institute, hone the personality, they also inculcate in students the ability to break down complex problems, assess choices and communicate solutions in a simplified, structured manner. The professional grooming, along with sophisticated problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, is responsible for making MBA graduates attractive to potential recruiters.

Despite global economic headwinds, the popularity of MBA programmes shows no sign of fading. A recent study by the Graduate Management Admissions Council (GMAC) analysed admissions data for over 100 MBA programmes globally and reported that more than 50% of schools noted an increase in admission applications. But, according to Dr. Salunkhe, “The real reason why MBA programmes are so popular lies beyond the numbers.” He credits the adaptability of MBA programmes for their success. By recognising the type of manager a market needs, institutes adjust their MBA programmes on a regular basis, in order to ensure their relevance and utility. “The management institutes will keep pace with the ever-changing markets and ensure that the MBA enthusiasm stays strong in the future,” predicts the [**Welingkar**](http://www.udaysalunkhewelingkar.net/welingkar-institute.php) Director.
